An independent certificate (workspace branches/b27ad439-4cea-4abd-b145-0a7ff4896b6c/pairmask_check.py, run with Python 3) intersected, over every pair of locations, the families of detector masks containing a distinguishing detector pair. It recovered both 17-coefficient arrays over all 65,536 masks per graph. Independent traversal gave 1728 vertices and 22176 edges for Shrikhande, and 2112 vertices and 30624 edges for rook, with both connected and every eccentricity five. An additional obstruction-mask calculation confirmed the four maximal-failure counts for each graph. The description of the rook witness in RESULT.md line 62 has a nonmaterial wording slip: for two selected rows, the indistinguishable vertices are in the same column in the two unselected rows (and transpose for selected columns). The two traces both consist of the two selected squares in that column; the exterior signatures coincide. In fact only adjacent exterior pairs with identical traces can collide at size eight or greater; the common equal-adjacency mask has size eight for adjacent pairs and six for nonadjacent pairs, while unequal flat traces and detector–exterior collisions can only occur at smaller sizes. The C++ file prints radius, diameter and eccentricities rather than asserting them; the frozen Python checker does assert them and the independent calculation supplies the check. The Bernoulli substitution preserves the exact coefficient difference and clears denominators to the strictly positive expression stated. No uploaded program was executed.
